messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Urgent: Fixed item parameters error
parts:
The portion here:

 sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name=="a1"),"value"] <- Fixed[i, "a"]
 sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name=="d"),"value"] <- Fixed[i, "b1"] 

Are you replacing intercepts (d) with the classical difficulty parameters (b)? If so, the ordering will be backward and probably not correct in terms of magnitude. This post might help, but given that this is undocumented it may be harder to follow: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!search/traditional2mirt/mirt-package/HaECnkrvV-E/qrR0dyy3BAAJ

Phil


On Mon, Jun 18, 2018 at 12:57 PM Abdulrazzag Falah <razza...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello Phil!

I am working with data that has 2PL and graded items. I wanted to fix the parameters of for some items. I read your response in this post https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/mirt-package/C1NtZwbBSWU and I followed exactly the same steps. I changed the values of the parameters to the my fixed values and I changed the 'est' column to FALSE so that they do not get estimated. Here is the problem, before I changed these parameters, the model used to work normally and produce good results. However, after I passed the 'pars' argument to the mirt function, it throws this error: 
Error: Graded model intercepts for item 1 in group 1 do not descend from highest to lowest. Please fix


My fixed parameters are already in a data frame and each item has an itemID. Here is my code:

sv <- mirt(dat[,-1], model=1, pars = 'values')
Fixed <-data.frame(fixed parameters here)
for (i in 1:nrow(Fixed)) {
  if(Fixed[i, "NIS"]==2){
    sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name=="a1"),"est"]<- FALSE
    sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name=="d"),"est"]<- FALSE
    sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name=="a1"),"value"] <- Fixed[i, "a"]
    sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name=="d"),"value"] <- Fixed[i, "b1"]
  } else {
    sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name=="a1"),"est"]<- FALSE
    sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name=="a1"),"value"] <- Fixed[i, "a"]
    for (j in 1:(Fixed[i, "NIS"]-1)) {
      sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name==paste0("d",j)),"value"] <- Fixed[i, paste0("b",j)]
      sv[which(sv$item==Fixed[i,"itemid"] & sv$name==paste0("d",j)),"est"]<- FALSE
     
    }
  }
 
}

mod <- mirt(data=dat[,-1],model=1, method = "EM", SE=TRUE, quadpts = 60, technical = list(NCYCLES=c(1000,200)), pars = sv)
> mod <- mirt(data=dat[,-1],model=1, method = "EM", SE=TRUE, quadpts = 60, technical = list(NCYCLES=c(1000,200)), pars = sv)
Error: Graded model intercepts for item 1 in group 1 do not descend from highest to lowest. Please fix



Please, advise on how to fix this issue. Your help is much appreciated.

Yours,

Abdulrazzag

Abdulrazzag
